scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - the edge layer's error envelope is not machine-readable, and it is not shaped like the db layer's. Two concrete defects, both measured against the local edge runtime this session: (1) an edge function's error body is {"error": "<prose>"} with NO machine-readable `code` field, so a caller can only pattern-match English to decide what happened - while the SAME platform's db layer returns {code, details, hint, message} for every failure class (400 bad column, 404 unknown table, 401 no grant), which a client CAN branch on. One product, two incompatible error contracts. (2) a routing 404 (unknown function name) is returned as **text/plain**, so `res.json()` THROWS rather than yielding an error object - the caller's catch block sees a SyntaxError about unexpected token, not a 404, and any code that checks `data.error` never runs. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the layer behind the AI gateway, the orchestrators, OCR/voice capture and report generation. A client that treats db and edge errors alike - which the identical-looking `.error` property invites - will mishandle one of them, and the failure mode is the one this bank keeps finding: an exception swallowed into an empty render, indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing. LEFT OWED RATHER THAN GREEN, DELIBERATELY: the oracle asks that status and body AGREE and that the envelope be uniform, and it does not. Banking it green would be a false green; recording it owed with the diagnosis is the honest state. TO FINISH: return JSON for routing 404s (Content-Type application/json), and add a stable `code` alongside `error` in every edge error body, then re-walk. That is an edge-function change and belongs in a batched wave, not mid-walk.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: every response this page's reads receive carries the envelope shape its client expects
withdrawn_evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 21 read relation(s), 10 were probed live at the gateway (asset_nodes, equipment_reading_templates, hive_audit_log, hive_members, parts_staged_reservations, parts_staging_recomme).  PLATFORM RESULT: across 40 relations, ZERO envelope defects and ZERO status/body disagreements. The error envelope is well-formed - {code, message, details, hint} on every error body, 400 (not 500) for an unknown column, 406 with PGRST116 for a single-object read of 0 rows, and a Content-Range header whenever Prefer: count=exact is asked. The status always agrees with the body: no 2xx carries an error object and no 4xx omits a machine-readable code. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.

findings.title: QUALIFIED - invalid-but-present enum returns 200 (analytics-orchestrator accepts any phase)
findings.detail: QUALIFIED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SESSION - flagged rather than left standing. This row was banked on four edge probes: 400 naming a missing field, 400 from a second function naming a different missing field, 404 for an unknown function, and 200 for a successful run. That evidence holds. But it did NOT include an INVALID-BUT-PRESENT field value, and probing that afterwards found analytics-orchestrator returns 200 for ANY phase string - metrics, analyze, summary, phase1 all returned 200 with the invalid phase ECHOED BACK, plus period_days:90 and a generated_at, even though the function's own source recognises only report, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. So `phase` is validated for PRESENCE and never for VALIDITY. WHY THAT BEARS ON THIS ORACLE: a 200 returning a result for an input the function does not recognise is a response whose status claims success for a request that was not actually understood. My banked wording said 'no 200-carrying-an-error', which was true of the cases I probed and is not established for this one. I am recording the qualification rather than quietly leaving the green, because a row that a later measurement undercuts is exactly the drift this bank exists to prevent - and because the same session that earned the row found the counter-case. NOT WITHDRAWN, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled: the four probed cases genuinely agree, and the new case is better classified as an input-VALIDATION defect than a status/body disagreement - the body IS internally consistent with the 200 it carries. Whether an unvalidated enum should return 400 is a design call on the function, not a contradiction between its status and its body. If the next walk judges otherwise, withdraw this row with a false-green-withdrawn finding; the evidence for both readings is recorded here. TO FINISH: validate `phase` against the known set in analytics-orchestrator and return 400 naming the valid values (the function already returns 400 with a named field for absence, so the pattern exists); then re-probe the invalid-enum case and settle this row without a qualification. Per A15 no edit was made - the edit budget is closed and it belongs in the next batched wave.
findings.observed: phase=metrics|analyze|summary|phase1 all -> 200 with the phase echoed; source recognises only report|descriptive|diagnostic|predictive|prescriptive

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.asserts: every response this page's reads receive carries the envelope shape its client expects
withdrawn_evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 21 read relation(s), 10 were probed live at the gateway (asset_nodes, equipment_reading_templates, hive_audit_log, hive_members, parts_staged_reservations, parts_staging_recomme).  PLATFORM RESULT: across 40 relations, ZERO envelope defects and ZERO status/body disagreements. The error envelope is well-formed - {code, message, details, hint} on every error body, 400 (not 500) for an unknown column, 406 with PGRST116 for a single-object read of 0 rows, and a Content-Range header whenever Prefer: count=exact is asked. The status always agrees with the body: no 2xx carries an error object and no 4xx omits a machine-readable code. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.

A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, which asks the oracle's question in the two halves it actually has.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, which asks the oracle's question in the two halves it actually has. STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed. A page that writes two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them: a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between the two leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page that writes one table and lets a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic by construction, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants were checked against live data and ALL HOLD - the inventory running balance, transactions with no orphan item, every reply and every live safety post carrying its XP award row, no XP row outliving a deleted post unreversed, no staged reservation both consumed and released, one AMC briefing per hive per shift date, a scope item not completed twice, no project child outliving its project. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp, and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ROSTER-WIDE: 11 pages client-sequenced, 11 single-or-no-write. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT banked green even though nothing is broken today. The page writes asset_nodes + parts_staged_reservations; asset_nodes + parts_staging_recommendations; asset_nodes + pm_scope_items and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC that writes both. So the first clause of the oracle ('either lands whole or not at all') is false as a structural matter: a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. WHAT THE LEDGER SAYS IS THE OTHER HALF, and it is genuinely reassuring rather than decorative: every declared conservation invariant holds against live data, so no half-write has HAPPENED. But 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code - the same shape as a latent null-collapse that no row has triggered. Banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either the second write moves behind a trigger or an RPC (making it atomic by construction, which is what 11 of the 22 pages already do and what the control pair demonstrates), or a probe interrupts the page BETWEEN the two calls and shows the ledger invariant catching the resulting half-state - which would prove the second clause with teeth instead of by absence. ★CORRECTION TO THE STRENGTH OF THIS CLAIM, made after reading what the pairs actually are. The prover enumerates every PAIR OF RELATIONS a page writes and asks whether the database links them - a cartesian over the page's write set, NOT a list of observed co-writes. Most of these pairs are therefore not one logical write split in two: community_posts + community_reactions are two separate user actions, asset_nodes + inventory_items are two different edits, and hive_audit_log pairs with everything because it is appended alongside many actions. A HALF-WRITE IS ONLY POSSIBLE WHERE A SINGLE ACTION WRITES BOTH TABLES, which is a smaller set than the pair count suggests - the plausible ones on this roster are flows where one submit genuinely lands two rows (resume_documents + resume_versions on an upload; logbook + schedule_items when a planned item is completed; asset_nodes + logbook when an asset is created during capture). Which pairs those are cannot be read from pg_trigger; it needs the page's write FUNCTIONS traced. SO THE ROW STAYS OWED FOR A NARROWER REASON THAN THE PAIR COUNT IMPLIES: the page writes multiple tables with no DB linkage, which MAY permit a half-write on whichever action writes two - and the ledger shows none has occurred. This is not a claim that every listed pair is a live risk, and the distinction is recorded rather than letting a large pair count read as a large defect. CONCRETE NEXT SLICE: not 'add triggers', but trace this page's write functions, identify which single actions write two tables, and interrupt only those between the calls.

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_null_semantics.py - 286 client coalesce sites read out of the pages and joined against the SCHEMA, so each one is judged against whether its column can actually be NULL. ★THE ORACLE'S OWN EXAMPLE IS NUMERIC: 'NULL meant no cap in the DB and arrived as a cap of ZERO in the client'. So the sites are separated by what the substitution DESTROYS, not by how many there are: numeric-substitute (50) and boolean-substitute (3) turn an UNKNOWN into a definite value and are the real class; not-null-in-db (15) cannot fire because the column is NOT NULL; visible-placeholder (47) renders an em-dash or equivalent and is the CORRECT behaviour, not a defect; text-blank (171) collapses NULL to '' where both already render as nothing - a weaker concern, recorded but not charged as this oracle's failure. ★THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A REAL NULL, which is what stops a clean page from being a vacuous pass: the control column v_achievement_xp_log.source_id holds 77 live NULLs and is found. A detector that cannot see that cannot see any. ★AND THE LIVE COUNT IS SEPARATE FROM THE LATENT ONE: zero of these sites is misbehaving TODAY, because the columns concerned currently hold no NULLs (0/4, 0/95, 0/97 on the ones sampled). That is a fact about this dataset, not about the code - which is precisely why the structural reading is the one banked here, and why 'no NULL has appeared yet' is not recorded as safety. FOR THIS PAGE: 8 site(s) substitute a definite value for a possibly-NULL column, which is the exact shape this oracle names. Example: `rec.confidence || 0` - column `confidence` (double precision), nullable on parts_staging_recommendations, so an UNKNOWN would arrive as 0. Not misbehaving today only because those columns currently hold no NULLs, which is a property of the data and not of the code.

evidence.asserts: NULL means the SAME thing on both sides of the seam: a view boundary does not collapse a real NULL into a zero or a false, and a client does not substitute one silently. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - null_semantics walks every view boundary column and checks whether a NULL that exists today survives the crossing.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - no view boundary column collapses a NULL that exists today, with 13 latent (columns where the collapse is possible but no NULL is currently present to prove it, recorded as exposure rather than counted as safe). The instrument's own honesty is the reason this row rests on it: 53 client-side numeric/boolean substitutions are reported as CANDIDATES and explicitly NOT failed, because this gate does not adjudicate displayed-vs-computed - a `?? 0` in a sort comparator is fine while the same expression in a rendered figure would be the defect, and every live one read by hand so far was a comparator. A gate that failed all 53 would be unusable and one that ignored them would be blind; reporting them as candidates is what makes the PASS meaningful. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration under this claim still expires it.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_write_atomicity.py, asking the oracle's question in the two halves it has. STRUCTURE - WHO SEQUENCES THE WRITE, read out of pg_trigger and pg_proc rather than guessed: a page writing two tables through two awaited client calls has NO transaction around them, so a 500, a closed laptop or a dead network between them leaves the first applied and the second missing, and nothing errors afterwards. A page writing one table and letting a TRIGGER or an RPC write the second is atomic BY CONSTRUCTION, because one statement is one transaction. LEDGER - WHETHER A HALF-WRITE IS VISIBLE TODAY: 14 of 14 declared conservation invariants checked against live data and ALL HOLD. ★AND THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN ABLE TO SEE A LINK, which is what stops 'client-sequenced' from being a verdict about the tool: the control pair community_posts -> community_post_xp_awards is joined by the trigger handle_community_post_xp and the detector finds it. A detector that cannot see that link cannot see any link, and would report every page as client-sequenced. ★ROSTER: {"client-sequenced": 11, "single-or-no-write": 11}. FOR THIS PAGE THE STRUCTURE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ORACLE, so this is NOT green even though nothing is broken today. It writes asset_nodes + parts_staged_reservations; asset_nodes + parts_staging_recommendations; asset_nodes + pm_scope_items and the database does NOT link them - no trigger, no single RPC writing both - so a failure between the two client calls leaves the first applied and the second missing, silently. Every declared invariant holds against live data, which is genuinely reassuring, but 'has not happened yet' is a statement about this dataset, not about the code; banking it green would convert an absence of evidence into a guarantee. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the very functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

The exposure the gate reports rather than hides is the honest part: 11 pages sequence TWO writes client-side, which is structural risk (a tab closed between them leaves the second undone) and is recorded as exposure, not counted as a failure, because no half-write has actually occurred in the data. That distinction is the same one this platform learned the hard way from a one-sided ledger write that passed every guard - the difference between "this could come apart" and "this has come apart" decides whether you are hardening a path or repairing rows. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration or function under this claim still expires it, and replay re-earns it in one command instead of a browser session.

findings.title: FAILS: with 2 reads answered 500, this page renders **258 characters of text and says nothing about the failure** - no error sentence, no dash sentinel, no retry. This is the reliability surface - P-F intervals, Weibull fits, FMEA - so a silent blank is indistinguishable from a plant with no assets
findings.detail: FAILS: with 2 reads answered 500, this page renders **258 characters of text and says nothing about the failure** - no error sentence, no dash sentinel, no retry. This is the reliability surface - P-F intervals, Weibull fits, FMEA - so a silent blank is indistinguishable from a plant with no assets registered. A BLANK SURFACE IS NOT AN HONEST ANSWER. The oracle asks that a server fault be shown as a fault rather than as an empty result, and an empty screen is the most literal empty result there is: someone opening this page during a backend fault cannot tell it from a page with nothing in it. THREE PAGES IN THIS SAME SWEEP DO IT PROPERLY, so the instrument discriminates and the pattern exists in-repo: hive says 'Could not reach your hive. Check your connection and refresh the page, or rejoin using your invite code.'; inventory says 'Could not load your inventory - Stock levels are unknown right now, not zero.'; pm-scheduler says 'Could not load PM compliance - Overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero.' Each names the domain consequence rather than the HTTP status. TO FINISH: render the failure verdict and dash the tiles on the error path, in the shape those three pages already use. MEASURED BY FAILING EVERY READ AT window.fetch AND COUNTING WHAT THE PAGE DOES NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request is answered with a synthetic 500 (`{"code":"500"}`, Content-Type application/json) while `/auth/v1/` is left untouched so the session survives - so the page sees a server fault, not a dead network, and supabase-js resolves it into an error object exactly as PostgREST would. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. THE INJECTION HAD TO MOVE FROM THE TRANSPORT TO window.fetch, AND THAT MATTERS FOR TRUST. An earlier pass used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered real data - a registered service worker sits between the page and the transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. Every verdict from that pass would have been false, and the interception counter is the only reason it was caught rather than banked. AND THE READING IS GUARDED INSIDE THE EVALUATE: it refuses unless the auth token holds the expected uid, `location.pathname` still ends in this page's own file, and the body is NOT in the 13,000-16,000 char landing-page band. A previous unguarded pass returned byte-identical output for seven different pages - 14,677 chars of marketing copy - because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. Seven page-specific verdicts, all of them the landing page. The guard is not ceremony.

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED, AND THE DATA TO FIX IT IS ALREADY IN THE SEAM. asset-hub's sensor panel renders the reading 2.438 under a VIBRATION heading with NO unit anywhere near it. Vibration is measured in mm/s (ISO 10816 velocity) or in g (acceleration), and those differ by orders of magnitude - so 2.438 is either a healthy machine or one that should be stopped, and the screen does not say which. THE FIX NEEDS NO NEW DATA SOURCE: v_sensor_truth already exposes parameter, value AND unit as a triple - the seam carries the unit and the render drops it. Exposing it as a separate column is BETTER than a suffix baked into a string, because the unit travels with the datum and can differ per sensor; the page simply has to print it. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN TIDINESS: this is the reliability surface - P-F intervals, Weibull beta, FMEA RPN - and a technician reads a vibration figure to decide whether to intervene. A number whose scale is ambiguous is worse than a missing one, because a missing number prompts a question and an ambiguous one invites a guess. TO FINISH (batched per A15): render unit beside value in the sensor panel. The same panel should also state the reading's AGE, which is a separate finding already recorded against this page.

findings.detail: NOT PROVEN, AND THE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS - which is the difference between this row and an untouched one. tools/prove_units_visible.mjs was written this turn and is proven able to PASS (pm-scheduler and analytics judge real quantities and carry their units), so a gap here is a fact about the view, not about the tool. ★THE ORACLE IS CONDITIONAL BY DESIGN: IF THE LABEL NAMES A DIMENSION, THE VALUE MUST CARRY ITS UNIT. Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. So 'MTBF: 45' fails, 'MTBF: 45 days' passes, and 'Open Jobs: 9' is never asked. ★THIS VIEW RENDERED ZERO DIMENSION-LABELLED QUANTITIES ON ITS DEFAULT STATE, so the check ABSTAINS rather than passing. '0 failing' over 0 judged is exactly the vacuous green this bank exists to refuse - it would read identically to a page that had been thoroughly checked. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, both caught by disbelieving the output. (1) It first accepted only BARE digits, so any value already carrying its unit never entered the set - 21 of 22 pages reported '0 judged' on a platform that renders MTBF and OEE nearly everywhere. An implausible abstention is an instrument fault, not a finding. (2) It then failed analytics on 'total downtime = 717.9h' because the time vocabulary listed hr/hrs/hours but not a bare 'h'. An oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle. Both are fixed and recorded in the tool. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: drive this page's V2/V3 views open before scanning - the quantities that owe units here live behind a modal, a tab or a selected record, exactly as effect_visible needed the disclosure and the selection performed before it could see anything.

And the view had to be OPENED first through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, whose open paths are read from source - scanning asset-hub's default state judges nothing, because this page keeps its measured numbers behind the reliability workbench disclosure. ★FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED: toFixed(3) shows a sensor reading to 0.001 of its unit. An implausible abstention is an instrument fault; an oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 18 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED, AND THE DATA TO FIX IT IS ALREADY IN THE SEAM. asset-hub's sensor panel renders the reading 2.438 under a VIBRATION heading with NO unit anywhere near it. Vibration is measured in mm/s (ISO 10816 velocity) or in g (acceleration), and those differ by orders of magnitude - so 2.438 is either a healthy machine or one that should be stopped, and the screen does not say which. THE FIX NEEDS NO NEW DATA SOURCE: v_sensor_truth already exposes parameter, value AND unit as a triple - the seam carries the unit and the render drops it. Exposing it as a separate column is BETTER than a suffix baked into a string, because the unit travels with the datum and can differ per sensor; the page simply has to print it. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN TIDINESS: this is the reliability surface - P-F intervals, Weibull beta, FMEA RPN - and a technician reads a vibration figure to decide whether to intervene. findings.title: RESOLVED FROM INCONCLUSIVE TO A REAL FINDING, BY MEASURING GEOMETRY INSTEAD OF TEXT.
findings.detail: RESOLVED FROM INCONCLUSIVE TO A REAL FINDING, BY MEASURING GEOMETRY INSTEAD OF TEXT. An FMEA failure mode was created through the page's own path (saveFmeaMode, after the registry's own precondition: click a [data-node-id], open the fmea tab). It reached the database and was correctly attributed - stored asset_id equals the selected node. It is NOT VISIBLE to the person who created it. ★WHY THIS TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO SETTLE, and why the first two were untrustworthy. document.body.innerText did not contain the marker; #rel-panel-fmea.innerText DID. Both are explainable at once, because innerText on a HIDDEN element falls back to textContent - so a panel in the DOM but off-screen reports its text when queried directly and is skipped by a body traversal. Two text scans, two opposite answers, neither one evidence. I did not pick the one I preferred; I changed the instrument. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT: find every element whose own text carries the marker and ask the GEOMETRY - a box with width and height, display not none, visibility not hidden, opacity not zero. Result: 2 elements carry the marker and NOT ONE of them is rendered. The mode exists in the DOM and is on nobody's screen. CHECKED AGAINST THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVES rather than assumed: it is not a looked-too-early artifact (the page had rendered 3,680 characters, and the same result repeats after a reload); it is not a lost selection (re-selecting the SAME node and re-opening the fmea tab still yields nothing rendered); it is not misattribution (the row's asset_id matches, and that node now carries 4 modes). WHAT THIS COSTS A PERSON: they fill in a failure mode, severity, occurrence and detection, press Save, and the RPN they just authored does not appear in the list they are looking at. The natural reading is that it did not save - so they enter it again. This is the surface whose whole job is building an asset's failure picture, and a silent duplicate there corrupts the picture rather than just annoying the author. NOT AUTO-FIXED: whether Save should re-render the panel, re-select the tab, or scroll the new row into view is a UX decision with three defensible answers, and this bank records rather than chooses. The DB half is banked green separately - the write is sound; only its feedback is missing.

findings.detail: MEASURED BY ACTUALLY DOING IT, then RELOADING AND LOOKING AGAIN - and the reload is the verdict. The effect was produced through the page's OWN save path and read back with psql as postgres. ★WHY THE VERDICT RESTS ON WHAT SURVIVES A REFRESH, learned by being wrong twice. Judging the immediate render kept crediting the wrong element: report-sender's only rendered match was #toast - a receipt for the write - and voice-journal's was #current-transcript, the composer's live echo of the text just typed. I first excluded those BY NAME, which is a blocklist, and a blocklist only excludes what its author already thought of: 'toast' was caught, 'current-transcript' was not. AN ECHO CANNOT SURVIVE A REFRESH; A RECORD MUST. So the page is reloaded and the marker looked for again, and that is what decides. voice-journal proves the distinction in one line: the same text rendered in #current-transcript immediately and in #history-list after the reload - two entirely different claims, and only the second is the effect being visible. ★AND VISIBILITY IS ASKED OF THE GEOMETRY, NOT THE TEXT: every element whose own text carries the marker is found, then required to have a real box, display not none, visibility not hidden, opacity not zero. innerText on a HIDDEN element falls back to textContent, so a text scan cannot separate 'the person sees it' from 'it exists in the DOM' - which is exactly how asset-hub produced two opposite readings before this was fixed. THIS PAGE FAILS, and the alternatives were excluded rather than assumed. The mode reaches rcm_fmea_modes and is attributed to the selected asset, but NO element carrying it is rendered - not immediately, not after a reload, not after re-selecting the same node and re-opening the FMEA tab, on a page that had drawn several thousand characters. The natural reading is that it did not save, so they enter it again - and on the surface whose whole job is an asset's failure picture, a silent duplicate corrupts the picture rather than merely annoying the author. NOT AUTO-FIXED: re-render the panel, re-select the tab, or scroll the new row into view are three defensible answers and this bank records rather than chooses. evidence.checked: MEASURED INSIDE V2 (#rel-panel-fmea, opened through the shared dialog_targets registry), not at page scope - the numbers this view carries are RPN badges, and they exist nowhere else. The panel renders .fmea-rpn values 180, 168, 60. VERIFIED ACROSS THE WHOLE TABLE RATHER THAN THE THREE ON SCREEN, because the interesting question is not whether the visible ones happen to agree: rcm_fmea_modes holds 99 rows for this hive and 300 platform-wide, and rpn is distinct from severity*occurrence*detection on ZERO of them. Every S, O and D also sits inside the 1-10 scale - 0 out-of-range rows. ★AND THE REASON IT CANNOT DRIFT IS BETTER THAN THE ORACLE ASKED FOR, which is worth recording because it changes what a future walk needs to check. The oracle's sibling invariant wants RPN 'recomputed at render rather than trusted from a stored column that can drift from its factors', and the page does NOT recompute - asset-hub.html:2639 renders String(m.rpn) straight from the row. That would be the drift-prone shape, except that rpn is a GENERATED ALWAYS column: ((COALESCE(severity,0) * COALESCE(occurrence,0)) * COALESCE(detection,0)). The database computes it on every write, so no client - not the UI, not an import, not a direct SQL insert - can store an RPN inconsistent with its factors. Reading a generated column is not trusting a mutable cache; the invariant is enforced one layer BELOW the place the oracle expected to find it. THE SCALES ARE ENFORCED TOO, not merely documented: severity, occurrence and detection each carry CHECK (>= 1 AND <= 10). So this page's domain truth that 'the S/O/D scales are stated (1-10)' has a constraint behind it rather than only a label, and an RPN of 180 is decomposable by a reader into 6 x 6 x 5 with confidence that those are the real factors.

evidence.asserts: repeating an identical write does not create a second record, and the guarantee is enforced by a constraint rather than by the client
evidence.checked: PROVEN BY REPEATING THE WRITE, inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member. The same row - same primary key, same payload - was inserted twice in one transaction. The second attempt was refused: 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint logbook_pkey'. So a repeat cannot create a second record, and the guarantee comes from a CONSTRAINT rather than from client-side de-duplication that a double-tap, a retry, or an offline queue drain could outrun. WHY THE CONSTRAINT IS THE RIGHT PLACE FOR IT: this platform queues field-capture writes offline and drains them on reconnect, so the same logical write can genuinely arrive twice from two directions. A uniqueness guarantee that lives in the page dies with the page's assumptions; one that lives in the index holds for the queue drain, the retry and the second tab alike. VERIFIED CLEAN: 0 probe rows survived. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13. SCOPE: this settles the REPEAT of an identical write. It does not settle a second write with a DIFFERENT client-generated id representing the same intent - that is the offline-queue collapse question and lives on its own seam row.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - 3 of 3 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: approveAssetNode (listener-bound), saveFmeaMode (listener-bound), saveStrategy (listener-bound). THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 2 reads answered 500, **this page offers no retry control at all** - zero visible elements whose label or handler mentions retry or try-again. It also says nothing at all about the failure (258 visible characters), so the reader has neither an explanation nor a control. SO A READER'S ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL PAGE RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant means losing whatever was on screen and paying the whole load again on the connection that just failed. THE PLATFORM HAS THE PATTERN ALREADY, so this is unadopted rather than undesigned: community renders a toast reading 'Couldn't load the community feed. Check your connection and try again.' with a **Retry** button beside it, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 posts. Six of the seven pages measured in this sweep have neither. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that re-issues the failed read and is measurable as such - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That distinction is not hypothetical: it is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY FAILING EVERY READ AT window.fetch AND COUNTING WHAT THE PAGE DOES NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request is answered with a synthetic 500 (`{"code":"500"}`, Content-Type application/json) while `/auth/v1/` is left untouched so the session survives - so the page sees a server fault, not a dead network, and supabase-js resolves it into an error object exactly as PostgREST would. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. THE INJECTION HAD TO MOVE FROM THE TRANSPORT TO window.fetch, AND THAT MATTERS FOR TRUST. An earlier pass used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered real data - a registered service worker sits between the page and the transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. Every verdict from that pass would have been false, and the interception counter is the only reason it was caught rather than banked. AND THE READING IS GUARDED INSIDE THE EVALUATE: it refuses unless the auth token holds the expected uid, `location.pathname` still ends in this page's own file, and the body is NOT in the 13,000-16,000 char landing-page band. A previous unguarded pass returned byte-identical output for seven different pages - 14,677 chars of marketing copy - because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. Seven page-specific verdicts, all of them the landing page. The guard is not ceremony.

findings.title: MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean.
findings.detail:
MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:False. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

Telling someone to check their connection is advice; a control they can press is a path, and the oracle asks for the second. The fix is to route this read's error branch through whListError, which this roster already uses on six pages - a per-path edit, not a design decision.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

findings.detail: FAILS BOTH CLAUSES. The oracle: 'when the primary is down the fallback engages and the surface says which it used, rather than pretending nothing happened.' Two clauses, and this page is measured against both. MEASURED with 2 reads answered 500 under the guarded probe: the page renders **258 characters and says nothing whatsoever about the failure** - no fallback, no error sentence, no dash sentinel, no retry control. This is the reliability surface - Weibull fits, P-F intervals, FMEA - so a silent blank reads as a plant with no assets registered. PRETENDING NOTHING HAPPENED IS EXACTLY WHAT A SILENT SURFACE DOES. The reader cannot distinguish a backend fault from a genuinely empty plant, and the page offers no way to find out. THE SWEEP DISCRIMINATES, so this is the page and not the probe: hive answers the same injection with 'Could not reach your hive. Check your connection and refresh the page, or rejoin using your invite code.', inventory with 'Stock levels are unknown right now, not zero', pm-scheduler with 'Overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero.' THERE IS NO READ FALLBACK ON THIS PLATFORM, AND THAT IS PROVEN FROM THE SERVICE WORKER'S SOURCE RATHER THAN INFERRED. `sw.js` handles API traffic in one branch - `if (url.includes('supabase.co') || url.includes('fonts.goog') ...) e.respondWith(fetch(e.request).catch(() => new Response('', { status: 503 })))` (sw.js:195-200) - so a failed read resolves to an EMPTY 503 body. And `cache.put` appears **nowhere in the file**, so no API response is ever stored: `caches.match()` cannot hit for a `/rest/v1/` URL because nothing put one there. The 26-entry `SHELL_FILES` precache holds HTML, CSS and JS only. SO THE FIRST CLAUSE CANNOT BE SATISFIED FOR READS BY CONSTRUCTION - there is nothing to engage. The offline layer this platform does have is for WRITES (the `wh_logbook_offline` / `wh_dayplanner_offline` / `wh_assethub_offline` IndexedDB queues), which is a different oracle. That makes the second clause the whole test: does the surface say the primary is down, or does it pretend nothing happened? MEASURED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, so the reading does not rest on one injection style. (1) Every `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request answered with a synthetic 500 at `window.fetch`, `/auth/v1/` left alone so the session survives, interceptions counted and a zero-interception run refused as vacuous. (2) A genuine `setOffline(true)` navigation with the service-worker cache WARM. THE SECOND METHOD TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO GET HONEST, WHICH IS WHY IT IS TRUSTWORTHY NOW. Navigating to `/workhive/logbook.html` offline served the branded offline shell every time - not because the page is unavailable offline, but because `SHELL_FILES` precaches ROOT paths (`/logbook.html`) and the `/workhive/` prefix is a different cache key. Measured at the path the cache actually holds, the real page is served. A verdict from the prefixed path would have described a cache miss and called it product behaviour. AND ONE LIMIT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: under Playwright's `setOffline(true)`, `navigator.onLine` still read **true** and `wh-conn-chip` still read 'Online' (hidden). The app's own offline DETECTION therefore never fired, so this reading covers 'the primary is down' but NOT 'the app knows it is offline'. The absence of an offline banner is consequently NOT charged against the page here. A probe that wants that claim must also override `navigator.onLine` and dispatch the `offline` event.

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its hero tiles while the reads are still pending.** With 6 reads in flight and none resolved, the observer recorded 40 server-derived numeric writes, including `ah-total-hero` = 0, `ah-critical-hero` = 0, `ah-pending-hero` = 0, `stat-logbook` = 0 and `stat-pm` = 0. THE STAKES HERE: asset-hub is the reliability surface (P-F intervals, Weibull, FMEA RPN) and the zeros it paints are `ah-total-hero`, `ah-critical-hero`, `ah-pending-hero`, `stat-logbook` and `stat-pm` - total assets, CRITICAL assets, pending approvals, logbook and PM history. '0 critical' on the asset-criticality screen is the single most consequential false zero in this set. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached those elements before the data existed. Four pages in the same wave passed the identical test (project-report, analytics, resume, assistant wrote no server figure at all while waiting), so this is a property of the page, not of the probe. THIS IS ONE INSTANCE OF A PLATFORM-WIDE PATTERN, now measured on all 22 pages: **six surfaces stamp 0 into hero tiles during load** - asset-hub, report-sender, shift-brain, skillmatrix, achievements and logbook - while fourteen do not. The shape is identical each time (a `*-hero` element written at resolvedAt === 0), which makes it one fix repeated, not six investigations. TO FINISH (batched per A15): hold the skeleton or write the dash sentinel until the read resolves. alert-hub is the reference implementation - 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that moment - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; every page in this wave returned controlOK = true. THE CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION - one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. THE ORACLE IS 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written', not 'were numbers written': writes to the local offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth needing no read), decorative stage numerals and engineering-design's static catalogue `pill-count` are classified separately and excluded.

findings.title: CLASSIFIED WITH EVIDENCE rather than left un-attempted.
findings.detail: CLASSIFIED WITH EVIDENCE rather than left un-attempted. This oracle asks that offline the write be REFUSED before firing and the person told nothing was sent - so before it can be graded, this view's committing write has to be identified and its CLASS settled, because the platform deliberately splits them: field capture QUEUES, while approvals, locked, financial, moderation and role writes are online-only-with-clarity (the generic drain carries no optimistic lock and those writes depend on one). Grading a queue-backed write against a refusal is wrong in both directions - green credits a refusal that must not exist, red calls a working feature a defect. The test is per-FUNCTION, not per-page: inventory, community and skillmatrix each show BOTH classes on one page. See PAGE_TESTBANK_ROADMAP.md SS6 for the sibling offline_queued cell proposed for the queue side, and tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs which grades it. THIS VIEW IS QUEUE-CLASS. Its write is registered with the page's own offline queue (window._whAhFmeaQueue over wh_assethub_offline, table rcm_fmea_modes), so offline it is HELD and the person is told it will sync - which is the correct behaviour and the opposite of what this oracle asks for. Refusing it would remove offline capture from someone working with no signal, which is the mistake I made on community's submitPost this session and had to revert after it removed working offline posting. WHAT THIS ROW NEEDS INSTEAD: the offline_queued oracle - zero server writes, POSITIVE acceptance evidence (the queue store grew), the will-sync message, no false refusal wording, and on reconnect a drain that happens EXACTLY ONCE. NOTE THE SPLIT ON THIS PAGE: saveFmeaMode rides the queue, but approveAssetNode and saveStrategy do NOT - approving an asset carries an optimistic lock (.eq status='pending') that a queued write would lose, and a strategy GENERATES pm_scope_items, the approval class. Both were guarded this session with whRequireOnline. Same page, both classes.

observed.same_page_refusers: approveAssetNode (optimistic lock) + saveStrategy (generates pm_scope_items) - both guarded this session

evidence.checked: driven offline and the ONLINE-ONLY write attempted - the RCM strategy save, chosen deliberately because this page ALSO has queued writes (rcm_fmea_modes is an offline-queue adopter) which this oracle does not govern. Pressed via #rcm-save, bound to the HANDLER (asset-hub.html:2908 assigns save.onclick = saveStrategy), reached through three MEASURED gates: #asset-view-toggle reveals #reliability-card, [data-node-id] selects an asset, then 'Edit strategy' opens the modal. 0 mutating requests left the page and the surface SAID SO; saveStrategy refuses at asset-hub.html:2929 via whRequireOnline before firing

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed. ★THE INDUCTION IS TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL, AND THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER. The availability lens fails a SUBSET of reads and reported 'affordances: 0' for pages that demonstrably DO render a Retry on other paths. Failing every request is what actually reaches a page's error branch. ★AND BOTH CLAUSES ARE MEASURED, because the second is the one that ships broken: a retry must RE-ATTEMPT and the failure must CLEAR. hive proved why - its first fix sent 3 fresh reads and left the page byte-for-byte unchanged, because it re-rendered from a cache still holding the failed state. A retry that re-attempts and does not recover is worse than none: it invites pressing again. ★THE ROSTER, so no page's verdict rests on its own reading alone: PASS 6 (hive, logbook, inventory, skillmatrix, public-feed, resume) | NO-RETRY 9 | NO-RECOVER 3 | NO-ATTEMPT 1 | SILENT 3. ★THE COMPONENT ALREADY EXISTS - THIS IS ADOPTION, NOT DESIGN. whListError(el, message, onRetry) in utils.js renders the inline error WITH a working Retry, and 16 pages already import it. Six pages passing is what separates 'nobody built this' from 'not every read path routes through it'. FOR THIS PAGE: it SAYS a failure happened and offers NOTHING TO PRESS. Telling someone to check their connection is advice; a control they can press is a path, and the oracle asks for the second. The fix is to route this read's error branch through whListError, which this roster already uses on six pages - a per-path edit, not a design decision.
